mike_sales: Heads-up - large POC (FinTech) hitting a hard blocker on our Private deployment. Their SOC says TLS sometimes fails and the app reports HTTP/502 with large cert chains. Need a swarming session ASAP, renewal meeting Friday.
mike_sales: symptoms: intermittent 502s, client logs show 'handshake failure' and our edge shows 502 upstream. Also they saw 429s during retries.
julia_se: is this via their site-to-site VPN to our colo private appliance or via their MPLS?
mike_sales: site-to-site IPsec to our co-lo appliance. They have NAT/lockdown at perimeter.
mike_sales: paste from their curl test: ```
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 10.8.9.21 (10.8.9.21) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake failure: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
* Received HTTP/2 stream 0 was not closed cleanly: INTERNAL_ERROR (err 2)
* Closing connection 0
```
omar_neteng: classic MTU/MSS problem on IPsec tunnels — large TLS handshake (cert + chain) gets fragmented and middlebox drops it. Also watch out for PMTUD disabled over IPsec.
omar_neteng: ask them to run: `ip link show` and `ping -M do -s 1400 <peer>` to test. If ping with don't fragment fails, their tunnel MTU is too small.
julia_se: also request `openssl s_client -connect 10.8.9.21:443 -servername api.poc.fin.example -showcerts` and a tcpdump of the handshake.
tara_support: I’ll open a PRIVATE ticket and add prebuilt checklist for customers with IPsec: MTU, MSS clamp, NAT, SNI preservation.
lucy_security: security note for questionnaire: we need confirmation that customer-managed perimeter does not TLS-terminate or perform TLS interception for Private deployments. Please add that constraint to the POC runbook.
mike_sales: they ran `openssl s_client` and got: ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
139000000000000:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca:SSL alert number 46
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
```
omar_neteng: that verify error is typical if their CA chain isn't present locally. But the alert implies the server side closed. Have them try MSS clamp as temporary: `iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` on their firewall or set tunnel MTU to 1400.
mike_sales: they applied MSS clamp and re-ran health check -> `curl -v --resolve api.poc.fin.example:443:10.8.9.21 https://api.poc.fin.example/health` now returns HTTP/200 consistently.
mike_sales: customer: "MSS clamp fixed the issue, TLS handshakes stable."
lucy_security: marking this in the questionnaire response: "Private on-prem package requires customer-managed network to preserve full TLS handshake; we recommend MSS clamping if IPsec."
billing_bot: customer asked about cost for a short Dedicated instance for predictable throughput during the POC. I've generated a rough estimate and assigned to finance: Q-7902.
tara_support: ticket PRIVATE-POC-458 created and assigned to julia/omar.
julia_se: leaving notes for runbook: include iptables snippet, MSS=1400 suggestion, and troubleshooting steps. Will draft a short KB.
mike_sales: closing convo for now — network fix applied, follow-up on pricing & legal. Thanks everyone.
